security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, ordinary Python imports, error messages, official service URLs, and a plain-text Chinese document. The implementation has genuine risks from non-atomic token permissions, unpinned runtime dependencies, direct destructive commands, and disclosure of the local hostname during OAuth registration.

remediation.issue: The OAuth token is written before file permissions are restricted.
remediation.suggestion: Create a temporary file with mode 0600, write and flush the token, then atomically replace the destination.

remediation.issue: Runtime dependencies use open-ended minimum versions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed dependency versions and publish a lockfile or hash-verified dependency set.

remediation.issue: Delete commands perform remote changes without an interactive safeguard.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation or a deliberate force flag for project, task, and focus deletion.

remediation.issue: OAuth dynamic registration includes the local hostname in the client name.
remediation.suggestion: Use a generic client name by default and make hostname disclosure an explicit option.

semantic_findings.title: OAuth Token Permissions Are Applied After Writing
semantic_findings.description: The access token is written before chmod applies mode 0600. On multi-user systems, the process umask can briefly expose a tasks:read and tasks:write bearer token.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code visibly calls write_text before chmod, so restrictive permissions are not established atomically.

semantic_findings.title: Runtime Dependencies Are Not Reproducibly Pinned
semantic_findings.description: The executable script requests dependencies with minimum versions only. Future invocations can install newer, unreviewed package releases and execute their installation or runtime code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The uv script metadata contains four greater-than-or-equal dependency constraints and no reviewed exact versions.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Commands Lack Programmatic Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: Project and task delete commands immediately call the remote deletion API. The skill asks the agent to confirm intent, but the CLI does not enforce that safeguard.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented confirmation rule is clear, while both command handlers delete immediately without a prompt or force option.

content.user_title: Manage TickTick Tasks from the Command Line
content.value_statement: Managing TickTick data manually can interrupt automated workflows. This skill uses the official Open API to manage projects, tasks, focus records, and habits.
actual_capabilities: Authenticate with Dida365 or TickTick through OAuth and a loopback callback.
List, inspect, create, update, and delete projects.
Create, update, complete, delete, move, and filter tasks with checklist items and tags.
Get, list, and delete focus records by type and time range.
List, create, update, and check in habits using structured fields or payload files.
limitations: The CLI requires uv, Python 3.14 or newer, network access, and supported Open API availability.
OAuth credentials are stored in a local token file and must be protected.
Account region is selected during login and later inferred from stored token metadata.
Delete operations have no CLI confirmation or undo support.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Personal Task Queue
use_cases.description: Review active tasks, add due dates, complete finished work, and move tasks between projects.

use_cases.title: Automate Project Intake
use_cases.description: Create projects and structured tasks from an approved workflow while preserving tags, priorities, and checklist items.

use_cases.title: Analyze Productivity Records
use_cases.description: Retrieve focus sessions, completed tasks, habits, and check-ins for a selected reporting period.

prompt_templates.title: List My Projects
prompt_templates.prompt: List my TickTick projects. Return each project name and identifier. Do not change any data.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Structured Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a task named [title] in project [project]. Set due date [date], priority [priority], tags [tags], and checklist [items].
prompt_templates.scenario: Create one task with common fields

prompt_templates.title: Review and Reorganize Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find incomplete tasks in project [source] with tag [tag]. Propose moves to project [destination], then wait for my approval before changing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a multi-task reorganization before execution

prompt_templates.title: Build a Productivity Summary
prompt_templates.prompt: For [date range], compare completed tasks, focus sessions, and habit check-ins. Group results by project and highlight missing or inconsistent records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced analysis across several API resources

output_examples.input: List my projects without changing anything.
Create a task called Submit expense report in Finance, due Friday, with two checklist items.
output_examples.output: Created Submit expense report in Finance. Due Friday. Checklist: gather receipts; attach approval.
Deletion can remove remote project data. Please identify the project and confirm that deletion is intended.

best_practices: Use read-only list or get commands to verify identifiers before remote changes.
Request JSON output when another tool or agent must parse the result.
Confirm the exact target before every delete, move, complete, or bulk update operation.
anti_patterns: Do not expose, print, or share the local OAuth token file.
Do not infer a project or task identifier from a similar display name.
Do not execute destructive operations from an ambiguous or indirect request.

faq.question: Which services does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Dida365 in China and the international TickTick service through their Open API endpoints.

faq.question: How does authentication work?
faq.answer: The CLI uses OAuth with PKCE, dynamic client registration, and a loopback callback on 127.0.0.1.

faq.question: Where is the token stored?
faq.answer: The default path is ~/.config/ticktick-cli/token.json. TICKTICK_TOKEN_FILE can select another path.

faq.question: Can it manage checklist items and tags?
faq.answer: Yes. Task create and update commands accept repeated items, structured item payloads, and repeated tags.

faq.question: Does it confirm deletions automatically?
faq.answer: No. The agent must obtain clear user confirmation before running project, task, or focus deletion.

faq.question: What is required to run the CLI?
faq.answer: The script declares uv execution, Python 3.14 or newer, four Python packages, network access, and a supported account.
